newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar breaks resistance in solid volum.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar breaks resistance in solid volum.

text.p: London's August white sugar contract finally pushed over $320 resistance on Wednesday after a combination of nearby spread deals and outright buying, traders said on Wednesday.
August and October were the most active positions, in mostly outright but also some spread trading. Limited crossed and against actuals trades were also seen.
By 1145 GMT August stood $1.30 higher at $320.20, just 30 cents off its intraday high, with a leading commission house cited as a good buyer.

Second-month October commanded more interest than in recent days, attracting a mixed bag of trade and brokers on both sides of the market. August/October was trading within a steady range between $10 and $11.

October was up $1.10 at $309.70 and overall volume reached 793 lots. Traders said the volume was better than expected considering the absence of major players due to Wednesday's Sugar Dinner in New York.
Paris trading was confined to the two nearby months in a total volume of 199 lots.
August was up $1.80 at $320.30 and October up $1.50 at $310.00.

In fundamental news, German analyst F.O. Licht cited unidentified Cuban sources saying Cuba's sugar production could be no more than 4.2 million tonnes tel quel in 1996/97, down from 4.45 million the previous year.
Pakistan said it expected 1997/98 output to jump to 3.0 million tonnes to 3.0 million tonnes from about 2.38 million the previous season, due to a higher acreage.
Pakistan has also raised raised its cane support price to boost domestic output and save foreign exchange.
